sectors.name: Banks
thesis: Our analysis: firm domestic activity supports credit demand, while large diversified banks retain funding and risk-management advantages.
A neutral policy stance makes deposit pricing, asset quality and margin discipline more important than a simple rate-cut thesis.
Prefer scaled franchises and improving challengers; avoid treating all lenders as homogeneous.

positive: Credit costs stay benign while growth remains broad-based.
negative: Deposit competition or unsecured stress weakens margins and asset quality.

sectors.score_methodology: Our analysis: 1-10 factor scores; weighted sum divided by 10 gives a 0-100 attractiveness score. Downside-risk score is higher when downside protection is stronger.

sectors.name: Information Technology
thesis: Our analysis: sector balance sheets and cash generation are strong, but global discretionary demand visibility remains uneven.
Price correction improves the setup selectively; it does not substitute for verified earnings revisions.
Prefer vendors with differentiated digital, engineering or platform capabilities and resilient client relationships.

positive: AI-led transformation spending converts to scalable revenue faster than feared.
negative: Pricing pressure and automation reduce labor-arbitrage growth before new demand scales.

EV transition creates opportunities but raises capital-allocation and competitive risks.

positive: Replacement demand and premium mix remain stronger than expected.
negative: Affordability pressure, discounting or transition spending dilute returns.

sectors.name: FMCG
thesis: Our analysis: strong franchises offer balance-sheet resilience and pricing power in a volatile macro environment.
Food inflation is a near-term risk to rural real incomes and input costs, so volume recovery should not be assumed.
The trailing correction improves selectivity, especially where execution and distribution remain strong.

positive: Rural volumes recover while input costs stabilize.
negative: Food inflation persists and price increases weaken volumes.

Prefer businesses with specialty, domestic brand or hospital execution rather than undifferentiated exposure.

positive: Specialty launches and domestic demand sustain growth beyond current expectations.
negative: Regulatory actions or price erosion offset operating leverage.

Use a barbell of regulated cash flows and disciplined integrated operators.

sectors.name: Capital Goods and Infrastructure
thesis: Reported budget policy sustains a large public-capex envelope; our analysis favors firms with execution capacity and order quality.
Private-capex crowding-in is upside, but should not be assumed without evidence.
Valuation discipline is essential because expectations for order growth are elevated.

positive: Private capex broadens and execution converts backlog into cash flow.
